options.text: She has been working here for 2020.
She has been working here since 2020.

questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous with 'since' plus a point in time (2020) is correct. 'For' is used with durations, and the other options misuse the tense.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'Each of the students ___ submitted the assignment.'
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so it takes the singular verb 'has' regardless of the plural noun that follows.

options.text: Neither the manager nor the employees were informed.
Neither the manager nor the employees was informed.
Neither the manager or the employees were informed.
Neither the manager nor the employees is informed.

questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Employees' is plural, so 'were' is correct, and 'nor' is the right correlative.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'If I ___ you, I would accept the offer.'
questions.explanation: In a hypothetical conditional, the subjunctive 'were' is used with all subjects, so 'If I were you' is correct.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct preposition: 'She is good ___ mathematics.'
questions.explanation: The idiomatic phrase is 'good at' when describing skill in a subject or activity.
